candidates.quote: The algorithm first produces a short list that is likely to contain the winning column and then checks each listed column.
candidates.what_precedes: The opening imports the circuit, decoder, local-test count, and all-input cap from §§3–4 and states the target upper bound. It then gives a conceptual two-stage summary and a link-based reading route. The executable stopping and acceptance rules arrive separately at lines 2443 and 2599–2616, after the detailed amplifier and ideal tournament.
candidates.reader_obstacle: The conceptual overview does not yet give a reader one complete program whose correctness the subroutine proofs are serving. In particular, amplification failure has opposite meanings in list generation and certificate checking. A chronological reader carries this unresolved control flow through the long state and drift calculations. This is an orientation issue, not an absent mathematical proof: lines 2610–2616 eventually explain the two meanings explicitly.
candidates.action: Insert one short whole-algorithm block at the end of the §5 opening, using named subroutines whose contracts are proved below. State the fixed T-stage horizon; keep only the classical pivot list between stages; on stage-sampler failure return the current list; decode each listed column afresh and fix that measured address; search for a failed exact local test; output one at the first candidate for which that search reports failure, otherwise zero. Identify both amplification calls by (gamma,eta), namely (1/(2m),epsilon) and (1/K,epsilon). Use the block to replace, rather than add to, the later duplicated control-flow summary.
candidates.why: This makes the acceptance event and the all-input stopping rule visible before their quantitative analysis. It also makes clear why neither the ideal weights nor an accurate address for every rival is an algorithmic input.
candidates.suggested_location: After line 2067, retaining the optional reading route at line 2069.

State f(L)<=epsilon only at the histories for which W(L)/m>=1/(2m). Then proceed to the coupling. Move the generic q_x(b) measured/reset discussion and its declaration-link distinctions to Appendix G.7, leaving one precise link here. Preserve the separate full-successful-state proof in §5.1.

It neither strengthens the sampler guarantee to all histories nor assumes independent stage failures.

candidates.quote: Its board uses Forrelation values $\Phi=+1$ and $-1$
candidates.what_precedes: §4.3 has specified a complete four-column board using Phi=+1/2, 0, and -1/2, with an explicit fill rule. §4.4 has derived the test list and soundness. Before applying its 371-test count to that board, line 1928 introduces the examples-first exposition and a second pair of nonzero Forrelation values; line 1930 directs an incoming reader back to that other account.
candidates.reader_obstacle: The second board is introduced in the middle of a single worked example in the lead account. The phrase four-column board at lines 1932–1939 then requires the reader to recover whether it denotes the board just defined in §4.3 or the companion board mentioned immediately before it. The text correctly warns that decoder laws differ, but that warning creates an avoidable board-identification task for someone reading only this document.
candidates.action: Let the local-test calculation continue directly from the named board of §4.3, explicitly calling it the §4.3 board. Move the alternate-board and return-to-exposition notice after the completed example, label it as a companion cross-reference, and state there that only the finite circuit and gate numbering are shared. Keep the Phi-dependent decoder laws tied to each separately named board. No numerical change to the 371 tests, 5936 input bits, or failed-test counts is proposed.
candidates.why: A worked example is most useful when the same concrete input persists across representation, local tests, and search probabilities. Stable naming prevents a source-convention warning from interrupting that chain or making accurate counts appear to apply to an unspecified board.
candidates.suggested_location: Keep lines 1932–1945 with a direct §4.3 identifier; relocate lines 1928–1930 after them or to a clearly separated companion-navigation note.
